# qunix

> An educational x86_64 macrokernel (monolithic kernel) written from scratch in Rust. It documents
> two things with evidence: where Rust stops helping once you are implementing the abstractions it
> normally protects you with, and which parts of kernel development actually benefit from AI
> assistance.

qunix boots UEFI via Limine, runs preemptive kernel threads across isolated address spaces, brings
every application processor online, and enters ring 3 through its own SYSCALL/SYSRET ABI. It is a
research kernel: no filesystem, no driver model, no network stack, no stable ABI.

Key findings, stated plainly:

- Rust contributes locality rather than immunity. A kernel's hard problems live inside `unsafe`
  blocks, where the borrow checker offers no guarantees. What the language provides is a bounded
  search space when an invariant check fails.
- AI assistance was most useful for breadth and for recalling architectural detail, and least
  reliable at judging whether a piece of validation was complete.
- Allocators do not fail loudly when they are wrong. Fuzzing surfaced real defects only once the
  harness stopped looking for crashes and asserted that no two live allocations overlap.
- A fuzz target that normalises its inputs cannot exercise the normalisation.

## Pages

- [Overview](https://quinnjr.github.io/qunix/): what exists, what Rust contributes, and the three
  findings that justified the approach.
- [Design decisions](https://quinnjr.github.io/qunix/design/): every non-obvious architectural
  choice with the constraint that produced it. Buddy allocator, slab heap, per-CPU state through
  GS, SMP bring-up, preemption ordering rules, owned address spaces, SYSCALL ABI, W^X.
- [vs Linux / OpenBSD / Redox](https://quinnjr.github.io/qunix/comparisons/): where qunix diverges
  from each and why, including where the established systems are simply right.
- [AI-assisted development](https://quinnjr.github.io/qunix/ai/): what worked, the categories of
  defect that needed machine-checked verification, and the three practices that caught them.
